chunks: And in it, that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except over those who follow him.
And He made for them partners in it to mislead them in knowledge. And they have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all.

key_terms.شُرَكَاءَ: Partners (referring to Satan's allies or aspects of his influence)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this conditional authority to refute the Mu'tazila and others who argued for Satan's absolute dominion, emphasizing that human free will (*ikhtiyar*) remains intact. This narration underscores the Shia theological principle that Satan acts as a persuasive guide (*dalil*) rather than a coercive force, misleading those who voluntarily align with his whispers through *zann* (speculation) rather than *ilm* (knowledge).
